reviews.title: “Search” is now “aura” and locked behind another sub
reviews.text:
Been using this app since 2019. Now, with the new AI “Aura” function, it seems that I can no longer search without being prompted for *another* subscription to enable aura. 

Example: when typing in “heart nebula” into the “Aura or search” bar, what do I get? A pop up to pay more money for Aura. No other search results

I guess I’ll go find a new app without AI slop and decreased features?

The developer’s response to the slew of other similar comments about unwanted and intrusive AI “features” doesn’t inspire confidence.

reviews.title: Persistent Info boxes = Programming 101
reviews.text: Saw all the impressive reviews. Wanted the integration with my Apple Watch so I could use it when using my ‘scope. App opened with a view so packed with stars that it was almost impossible to find known objects, and no way to adjust the view to my current conditions.  But worst of all, when I selected a known object like Saturn or Jupiter and brought up their info page, all of the dense detail that I would love to read would close in about 7-10 seconds. There’s obviously a lot of good info in there for someone interested in learning, if it would just stay open. And I get that you’re trying to make a living, but how about you lay off the subscription pop ups until I’ve had a little time to actually use the program for more than a few minutes. Not willing to subscribe until basic functions are supported.

reviews.title: Annoying as ever
reviews.text:
I don't remember when I first found out about this app; I've been using it in some way for upwards of ten years. Night Sky has changed a lot— it's moved from hip thing to hip thing, from AR to AI. Still, though, it has all of the same old problems it had years ago, with some new ones. 

What do I mean? Some of the controls are still oversensitive: tap the screen too quickly or too many times in succession, and you'll invariably zoom way, way in. On the other hand, the others are not sensitive enough: try tapping on the planet you want, and you'll probably end up just zooming in again or clicking something else on accident several times before you reach Jupiter, sometimes even when you're zoomed close to it. Those problems have always plagued this app, and they apparently always will.

(There's another one that's less of a performance issue, but I will mention it anyway. The information for every planet, star, and deep sky object is taken directly from  Wikipedia pages. That can be iffy in itself. However, many stars and objects will pull up a generalized page based on where they are often catalogued. For example, even some relatively well-known New General Catalogue galaxy may pull up the Wiki page for the NGC instead of a page for the object itself. This is frustrating if learning is your goal, not just finding.)

New additions to the app have brought new problems. I remember when Night Sky Plus came around (it's older than some reviews may suggest) and began throwing up a "

reviews.title: Enough with the popups
reviews.text:
I used to love this app. Used for nearly 10 years periodically as my go-to for amateur stargazing. Just returned to it after a feww months and man, gotta say the same experience is disappointing: 1) of course for seeing the inevitable leakage of ai into this, and 2) getting popup ads to buy premium+ai subscription is more than annoying, and makes the app truly useless… I can’t do a basic star search without getting this popup every couple seconds of its usage. Even worse, the popup freezes your screen when you don’t have any cell service, so the app is indeed useless.

I get it, you want people to upgrade. But I’ve already seen your offer. Obviously, if I wanted its features I’d buy it. Showing me the offer 20 more times won’t change that. Advertising this aggressively just pushes people away. And in my case, permanently. Hope your team can take a hint.

reviews.title: 4 Reasons
reviews.text:
1. The search function when you try to favorite something is broken, so I have to scroll through every object to find the one I want. Then when I do find it, I click it, then press the check button in the upper right corner and it does nothing. Then I just give up on that but it won’t let me exit the screen, so I have to close then reopen the app

2. There is WAY to much background noise. There should be a way to filter out ‘less important’ stars.

3. Too many popup ads. Whenever I accidentally open the search menu and I scroll down it immediately opens up the shop/store menu. You should just add a singular button to get premium, and add a “Don’t Show Again” button for the popups.

4. As a sci-fi fan, I want to look at (real) stars that I read about in my books. But when I searched up Tau Ceti, nothing appeared, as if it was non-existent.  

In conclusion, I think that this app has a lot of potential but is littered with bugs and has an annoying user interface.

reviews.title: Great idea ruined by greed
reviews.text:
Night Sky used to be a brilliant, simple stargazing app. Now it’s a bloated, paywalled mess. Locking something as basic as searching for a star behind a ~£70 per year subscription is frankly absurd. This is not Netflix or professional software. It’s a casual astronomy app.

The interface has become cluttered, the experience feels worse than earlier versions, and the value proposition is terrible. It feels like the app has been engineered to extract money rather than provide a good user experience.

Plenty of other apps let you search the night sky for free or for a small one-off purchase. This used to be one of the best. Now it’s just another example of aggressive monetisation ruining a good product.

reviews.title: Bloated and Not Intuitive
reviews.text: I’ve been using this app for years and in the last year, this app has become bloated and near non-functional. As an amateur stargazer, searching for satellites, constellations, or stars is neither intuitive nor helpful. This is particularly sad considering the extremely steep pricing system for the additional (non-helpful) AI. The amount of times in the last year that I have been attempting to locate a fleeting satellite and opened the app only for it to have multiple pop ups and animations that slow me down, causing me to lose the satellite is crazy-making. Last night alone, I was attempting to locate a very basic satellite and was routinely offered the upgrade with the AI version. I upgraded multiple times and it failed to upgrade. I was then stuck in a loop where I would attempt to continue to locate the satellite and the pop-up would then interrupt my search as if I didn’t already enroll. I lost the satellite AND had the pleasure of upgrading for nothing. While traveling in Australia, I wanted to locate the Southern Cross and it took me a solid 30 minutes of attempting to navigate the app to find one constellation. I work in tech and am exceedingly familiar with app screen design and the UI of this app has fallen off.

There is no way to turn it off in settings or within the app, and if you try to turn off your location to prevent it, bombard you with a turn on location notice every .5 seconds ultimately leading to you being unable to look at anything that isn’t visible with a naked eye

reviews.title: Used to love this app - ruined with AI
reviews.text: I am incredibly saddened to have to leave a review like this. I’ve been using the Night Sky app since 2020, and it has been immensely helpful in my journey of learning about astronomy, stargazing, and how to find constellations in the sky. I loved the inclusion of astronomy news and the several tools that came with the app - like notifications for when certain objects were rising in the sky. However, with the inclusion of a generative AI assistant in the app, I can no longer use Night Sky in good conscience. I am extremely disappointed that an app dedicated to science and understanding part of the natural world is using technology that has been clearly demonstrated to have both ethical AND environmental concerns, ESPECIALLY as light pollution is a growing issue being worsened by AI data centers. I am absolutely disappointed. Do better.

reviews.title: A shame
reviews.text:
UPDATE:

Developers have decided to turn a blind eye to what I said asking for a one time payment option like they previously offered (there was no reason to remove it unless greed). And they kept saying to use the free option but the only issue is I use the night sky app on both my iPhone and Apple TV. Lots of content on the Apple TV requires a subscription or payment of some sort which is why I wanted to purchase the one time only £229.99 option as it was cost effective for me and did exactly what I wanted. After seeing the developers response clearly stating they have no intent to bring back the one time purchase option I can only keep my one star review and delete the app. I have found other apps ironically cheaper that have one time purchases which I’ve now done so this developer has lost money from a potential sale all because of greed. The only downside to these other apps is they don’t have Apple TV app versions however this is a minor trade off in return for a one time payment. Such a shame as this used to be such a good app. Yet another thing ruined by subscription only payment models…
